title: Topic 7.2: Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading

pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 7.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: INDEPENDENT READING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.2: Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Why should we read different types of materials?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. read a variety of materials (narratives, poems, graded readers) for lifelong learning
2. demonstrate independent reading of a variety of materials (narratives, poems, graded readers) for information

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading

Teach
• Focus skill: read a variety of materials (narratives, poems, graded readers) for lifelong learning.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we read different types of materials?
2. What kind of materials do you enjoy reading?
3. What can you do to remember what you read?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
